papers.title: Prediction of Specific Energy Consumption in Sustainable Milling of Ti-6Al-4V with Different Machine Learning Models
papers.abstract: Research on eco-friendly and energy-efficient machining processes has gained significant importance within the domain of sustainable production. This study is focused on enhancing the energy performance and sustainability of the milling process. Four machine learning (ML) models, namely, multiple linear regression (MLR), support vector regression (SVR), Gaussian process regression (GPR), and adaptive network-based fuzzy inference system (ANFIS), were proposed to estimate specific energy consumption (SEC) in the milling of Ti6-Al4-V under two eco-benign cooling conditions: cryogenic and minimum quantity lubrication (MQL). Several statistical metrics, including normalized mean absolute error (nMAE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), normalized root mean square error (nRMSE), maximum absolute percentage error (maxAPE), coefficient of determination (R2), and Willmott’s index of agreement (IA), were employed to validate the performances of the ML models. A high level of agreement between the predicted and experimental SEC data for both the training and test datasets supports the reliability of the proposed ML models. Although the MLR model performed well, the results revealed that the other ML models demonstrated better overall performance. According to the statistical metrics, the models’ predictive performance improved in the following sequence: MLR, SVR, GPR, and finally ANFIS, which demonstrated the highest predictive capability.

summary_zh.motivation: 为实现可持续生产，预测钛合金铣削过程中的单位能耗。
summary_zh.method: 采用四种机器学习模型（MLR、SVR、GPR、ANFIS）对单位能耗进行预测。
summary_zh.result: ANFIS模型预测能力最高，MLR最差。
summary_zh.validation: 使用统计指标比较预测与实验数据验证模型可靠性。

summary_en.motivation: To enhance energy efficiency and sustainability in machining, this study aims to predict specific energy consumption during milling of Ti-6Al-4V.
summary_en.method: Four machine learning models (multiple linear regression, support vector regression, Gaussian process regression, and adaptive network-based fuzzy inference system) were developed to estimate SEC under cryogenic and MQL cooling conditions.
summary_en.result: The ANFIS model outperformed the others in predictive capability, while MLR showed the worst performance.
summary_en.validation: Model predictions were validated against experimental SEC data using multiple statistical metrics including nMAE, MAPE, nRMSE, and R².
